places.name: 近江町ラーメン (Omicho Ramen)
places.neighborhood: Omicho Market / Aokusamachi (Hokutetsu Kanazawa Stn)

noodles.notes: Custom-ordered thin, straight noodles (sourced from a specialty noodle maker) of 100% domestic wheat — a firm, smooth bite chosen to carry the delicate dashi-forward broth rather than fight it.

ramen.signature_bowl: 特製のどぐろラーメン (Special Nodoguro Ramen) — a clear shio-kaeshi broth built on a generous amount of nodoguro (blackthroat seaperch) bones simmered daily, layered with poultry stock for a refined, dashi-like umami.
ramen.chashu: Sources differ on the signature topping: the market's listing describes low-temperature braised pork (four slices), while the shop's PR coverage describes rare-cooked duck chashu — both are gently cooked, lean and refined rather than fatty/char-grilled, to match the delicate broth.

gf.note: Wheat-based noodles and a shoyu/shio tare are standard; no rice or konjac noodle or gluten-free seasoning option is documented.

vegan.note: Every bowl is built on fish (nodoguro) and/or poultry stock with animal-based tare and chashu; no documented plant-only broth option.

ramen.pantheon: A modern, refinement-driven bowl that channels Kanazawa's prized nodoguro (blackthroat seaperch) into a crystal-clear, dashi-like soup — you taste the luxury fish and clean poultry stock in every sip rather than any heavy regional lineage. It is a contemporary kaiseki-leaning take on light ramen, where restraint and the deep umami of premium local seafood are the whole point.

noodles.notes: Specially-formulated thick noodles (特製太麺) built to grab and balance the concentrated meat-juice sauce rather than carry soup. No documented detail on shape, hydration, or whether they are handmade.

ramen.signature_bowl: 極〆そば (Goku-Shime Soba) — the course-finishing thick noodles tossed in the rendered meat juices and the house sauce, ordered at the end of the grilled-meat meal.
ramen.chashu: None. This is a grill finisher, not a ramen — no chashu component is documented.
notable_toppings: soft egg / onsen-style egg (documented on the finishing noodles)

gf.note: Wheat thick noodles plus a miso/soy-style house sauce that almost certainly contains wheat — not safe for celiacs, and this is a yakiniku house with no documented gluten-free noodle option.

vegan.note: The entire dish is built on rendered beef/pork meat juices from the grill plus an animal-derived sauce and egg topping — there is no plant-based version.

ramen.pantheon: This is not a ramen bowl at all but the soul of a Kanazawa horumon house's grand finale: thick noodles dragged through the rendered fat and juices of premium wagyu and offal, dressed in a house white sauce and a multi-miso black sauce. It belongs to the brothless shime-soba / abura-soba lineage — you taste the grill, not a simmered soup.

noodles.notes: Medium-thick wavy noodles chosen to grab and carry the roasted-miso broth; they cling to the soup with a firm, satisfying bite.

ramen.signature_bowl: Miso Ramen (味噌ラーメン) — the house standard built on iron-pot roasted miso; black miso (squid-ink) and red miso (spicy) are the popular variations, with miso tsukemen for dipping.
ramen.chashu: Noto-pork chashu, prized for its quality; braised pork served as the bowl's centerpiece.

gf.note: Wheat-and-kansui ramen noodles plus a miso-and-soy tare; no rice or konjac noodle option is documented, so this bowl is not celiac-safe.

vegan.note: The broth is built on chicken bones, pork bones, chicken feet and dried sardine, finished with pork fat and pork chashu — no plant-based bowl is offered.

ramen.pantheon: A modern Hokuriku miso specialist where the soul is the miso itself: each serving is finished in its own iron pot so the paste chars and caramelizes, sending up a smoky, deeply aromatic fragrance over a chicken-and-pork broth lifted with niboshi and kombu. Bright accents of grated ginger, yuzu and green laver keep the rich, roasted miso from ever turning heavy, so the flavor shifts as you eat.

noodles.notes: Wheat-and-kansui noodles kept simple and restrained so as not to overpower the delicate, gently sweet broth. One cold variant was noted as medium-thickness wheat noodles with good firmness and bite.

ramen.signature_bowl: 中華そば (chūka soba) — the classic clear shoyu bowl; the menma-forward メンマラーメン showcases the house bamboo shoots, and the Kaga sake-kasu ramen (加賀酒粕ラーメン) is the local specialty worth seeking.
ramen.chashu: Lean, lightly braised pork chashu — a "healthy," restrained cut chosen to suit the gentle soup rather than a fatty, rich preparation.
notable_toppings: house-made menma (bamboo shoots reconstituted over three days, hand-kneaded and slow-seasoned — crisp yet tender)

gf.note: Wheat-and-kansui noodles and a soy-based (wheat) shoyu tare; no rice- or konjac-noodle or gluten-free tare option is documented.

vegan.note: The broth is built on chicken and fish (plus kombu and vegetables), and bowls carry pork chashu and egg; no documented plant-only (no katsuo/no animal) bowl.

ramen.pantheon: A quiet, old-school chūka soba in the heart of Kanazawa's market: chicken, fish, kombu and vegetables coaxed just below a boil into a crystal-clear, naturally sweet broth that tastes of restraint rather than power. It leans toward the gentle, gobō-clear lineage of Hokuriku market ramen, with a local twist in its Kaga sake-kasu specialty.

sweep_downgrade.why: The tsuyu's defining ingredient is 焼き鯖干し (grilled dried mackerel) dashi and the house bowl is 鴨せいろ (duck). Fish dashi is in the dipping sauce that arrives with every soba order, so there is no vegan path even by omission - 'no' is the honest label, not 'ask'.
